verdict.rationale: Lithic's Auth Rules engine can decide on a risk score at authorization time, at program, account or card level. Rules can be tested in shadow mode with backtesting, and ASA supports custom real-time approval decisions. That covers the auth-time fraud-scoring part of the story well, but the evidence does not show suspicious-activity alerting or tooling to block and reissue compromised cards. Missing for 10: documented suspicious-activity or fraud alerts, card block/pause and reissue tooling, and independent or hands-on corroboration of fraud effectiveness.

support.subject: As an ops user, the platform fights fraud on my issued cards — network fraud scores or its own models surfaced at auth time, suspicious-activity alerts, and tooling to block and reissue compromised cards

citations.quote: By defining rules based on high-signal attributes like MCC, country, currency, and risk score, you can enforce business-specific authorization logic at the program, account, or card level
Authorization Stream Access (ASA) provides the ability to make custom transaction approval decisions through an HTTP interface to the ISO 8583 message stream.
shadow mode lets draft rules observe the authorization stream without affecting outcomes, while performance reports and backtesting measure impact over time
